predecessors.name: French Third Republic
predecessors.text: The departments of Haut-Rhin and Bas-Rhin 'except for the city of Belfort and its territory', 'most of the French department of Moselle', one-third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck…

successors.name: French Third Republic
successors.text: Alsace-Lorraine, reoccupied by French troops from 22 November 1918 (Strasbourg) and recognised as French by the Treaty of Versailles in 1919

ledger.x: 28 June 1871: the German Empire creates the Imperial Territory of Alsace-Lorraine.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: German victory: Sedan (1-2 September 1870), Paris armistice (January 1871) and the Treaty of Frankfurt of 10 May 1871, by which France ceded Alsace (except Belfort) and most of Lorraine's Moselle ('the ceding of 1,694 French villages and cities to Germany')…

certainty.note: The Treaty of Frankfurt fixed the frontier village by village (1,694 villages and towns); Belfort, kept by France, is the exception that makes the line.
